page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m1.large is an entry-level, compute-focused virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture utilizing an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, paired with 2.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1.0 GB per core ratio. This instance does not include local storage or GPU hardware, relying entirely on external storage options, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate average single-core capabilities but overall constrained multi-core and memory performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU test shows average performance at 1834.58, and single-threaded compression tasks like gzip and bzip3 also perform in the average tier. However, multi-core CPU performance is poor, scoring 1918.98 on stress-ng, which is in the bottom 10% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only large block speeds at 15.64 GB/sec and write speeds at 13.95 GB/sec, both falling into the bottom decile.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a low-cost entry point for workloads that require dedicated CPU allocation but have minimal memory and storage demands. The primary tradeoff is the highly constrained 2.0 GB memory capacity and poor multi-threaded scaling, which limits its utility for memory-intensive or highly parallelized applications.

This server type is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded workloads, basic web serving, simple utility scripting, and small-scale development or testing environments that do not require high memory density or local disk performance.
